item.title: NAFDAC destroys 50,000 fake alcohol bottles in Lagos, uncovers raw ethanol
item.description: … Seizes branded bottles of Jack Daniel’s, Hennessy, Johnnie Walker By Chioma Obinna The National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC) has destroyed more than 50,000 empty branded alcoholic beverage bottles uncovered at Iyana Oba, Lagos State, in a major crackdown on the circulation of counterfeit alcoholic products. The bottles, which allegedly were stockpiled for supply to counterfeiters, carried the labels of popular alcoholic beverage brands, including Jack Daniel’s, William Lawson’s, Johnnie Walker Red Label and Blue Label, Action Bitters, Lord’s Dry Gin and Hennessy. NAFDAC Investigation and Enforcement officers, who discovered the stockpile, also found raw ethanol stored in a drum at the location, raising concerns about possible illegal production and packaging of alcoholic beverages using the branded containers. The agency said more than 50,000 assorted bottles were destroyed to prevent them from being recycled or reused in the production and distribution of counterfeit alcoholic products. The discovery has renewed concerns over the activities of counterfeiters who exploit the popularity of established alcoholic beverage brands by using their original packaging to deceive unsuspecting consumers. The practice poses serious public health risks, as consumers may unknowingly purchase and consume adulterated products whose contents, ingredients and production conditions cannot be verified. NAFDAC warned against the trade, storage and use of branded packaging materials for counterfeiting, stressing the need for vigilance and cooperation from members of the public. The agency also urged Nigerians to report suspicious activities involving the stockpiling, sale or distribution of branded bottles and other packaging materials to enable it to take appropriate enforcement action. It reiterated its commitment to protecting public health and preventing counterfeit and unwholesome products from entering the Nigerian market. item.title: ‘Teachers, doctors won’t pay tax when I become gov’
item.description: By Cynthia Alo & Kafayat Kokumo LAGOS — Lagos State governorship candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, Mr. Adedeji Doherty, yesterday, promised to exempt teachers and doctors from paying taxes, if elected governor, saying his administration will use increased Federal allocations to improve healthcare, education and welfare of residents. Doherty, who made the promise during an interview on a Channels Television programme, said he would also introduce a tax card that would enable residents unable to afford the existing tax burden to pay N10,000 annually and enjoy subsidies on drugs and transportation. He said: “When I am governor, I will transfer these palliatives, these subsidies to my people. For instance, the doctors will not pay tax. For instance, the teachers will not pay tax. Those two groups will not pay tax. “Out of this N250 billion plus, I will transfer it into cards, whereby for those that cannot pay N50,000 per year in tax, I will create a card that you can pay N10,000 per year in tax, but you will get a subsidy in your drugs and you will get a subsidy in your transportation. “This is giving money back to the people of Lagos State because I have it. Mr President has given it to me and I am giving it to you.” The PDP candidate also promised free education, saying the funds available to the state would enable him to implement the policy. Justifying the proposed tax exemption for doctors, he said: “We need close to about 15,000 doctors in Lagos State as we speak, but right now we have only about 3,000. So, if 3,000 doctors are not paying tax, please give me a break.” He described teachers as critical to the state’s future, arguing that they must receive proper training and support to prepare children for leadership and professional responsibilities. Doherty further condemned attacks on political activities and disclosed that some people he described as area boys had pulled down his campaign posters around Oregun and the Third Mainland Bridge. He said his Director-General had reported the incident to the police, adding that he would visit the Department of State Services, DSS. item.title: Vanguard loses Online Editor, Femi Ajasa
item.description: The Management of Vanguard Media Limited announces with profound sorrow, the death of its Online Editor, Mr Olufemi Finayon Ajasa, who passed away on Sunday at the Lagos University Teaching Hospital (LUTH) after a brief illness. He was aged 44. A statement from the Editor, Mr Eze Anaba, said his death is a massive loss to the Vanguard family and the journalism profession. Mr Ajasa was a valued member of the Vanguard family, who made significant contributions to the growth of the company’s digital operations and online journalism. Born into the Ajasa family of Ajido, in Badagry Local Government Area of Lagos State, Olufemi Ajasa obtained a Bachelor of Science degree in Mass Communication, specialising in Journalism, from Lagos State University between 2004 and 2009. He further honed his professional skills with a certification in Advanced Writing and Reporting Skills from the School of Media and Communication, Pan-Atlantic University, in 2015. He began his journalism career as a photojournalist with National Mirror Newspaper in February 2012, where he worked until November 2013. He joined Vanguard Media Limited in December 2013 as an online reporter and content developer, serving until September 2016. He subsequently moved to TheNewsGuru.com, where he worked from 2016 to 2021, first as Online Editor and later as Team Lead and Head of Digital Operations. In December 2021, he joined Pulse as Editorial Quality Assurance Manager. Ajasa returned to Vanguard in June 2022 as Online Editor, a position he held until his death. His return marked the continuation of a relationship with the organisation that began early in his professional career. The management of Vanguard Media Limited deeply regrets this irreparable loss and extends its heartfelt condolences to his immediate family, friends, professional associates and all members of the Vanguard family. At this difficult time, our thoughts and prayers are with his family. We pray that God grants them the strength and fortitude to bear this painful loss, and that the soul of our departed colleague finds eternal rest. The Service of Songs/Wake-Keep in honour of the deceased will hold at 14 Sylvia Crescent, Anthony Village, Lagos, on Thursday, November 19, at 5 p.m. Other funeral arrangements will be announced by the family May his gentle soul rest in perfect peace. item.title: Inflation rate drops year-on-year, rises month-on-month
item.description: By Elizabeth Adegbesan The National Bureau of Statistics, NBS, has disclosed that Nigeria’s headline inflation rate dropped to 14.06 percent in October 2026 from 14.63 percent in the previous month. NBS stated this in its latest Consumer Price Index, CPI, Report noting that food inflation also declined to 19.13 percent from 19.59 percent in September. However, Month-on-Month, MoM, inflation rate rose by 0.43% in October, up by 0.38 percentage point from 0.06 percent recorded in September 2026. This increase also reflected in the MoM trend in food inflation for October. NBS stated: “In October 2026, the Headline inflation rate stood at 14.06 percent, down from 14.63 percent in September 2026 and stood at 18.97 percent in the same month of the preceding year (October 2025). “Looking at the movement, the October 2026 Headline inflation rate showed a decrease of 4.9 percent compared to the October 2025 (18.97 percent) Headline inflation rate. “On a month-on-month basis, the Headline inflation rate in October 2026 was 0.43 percent, which was 0.38 percent higher than the rate recorded in September 2026 (0.06 percent). “This means that in October 2026, the rate of increase in the average price level was higher than the rate of increase in the average price level in September 2026.” On food inflation, NBS, said: “The Food inflation rate in October 2026 was 19.13 per cent on a year-on-year basis and stood at 16.3 per ent in the same month of the preceding year (October 2025). “However, on a MoM basis, the Food inflation rate in October 2026 was -0.75 percent , up by 0.80 percent points from September 2026 (-1.55 per cent). “This can be attributed to the rate of change in the average prices of the following products: vegetable oil (75cl), Titus sardines (125g), green peas (Prepacked), mackerel frozen, croakers (apo), rice local, catfish fresh, beef tripes, palm oil (75cl), millet flour (sold loose), etc” In October 2026, food inflation on a year-on-year basis was highest in Ondo (31.74 percent), Lagos (31.43 percent), and Imo (29.75 percent), while Nasarawa (3.7 percent), Bayelsa (7.11 percent) and Kano (7.13 percent) recorded the slowest rise in food inflation on a Year-on-Year basis. “On a MoM basis, however, October 2026 food inflation was highest in Yobe (18.41 percent), Kebbi (16.45 percent), and Borno (13.96 percent), while Lagos (-5.93 percent), Plateau (-5.83 percent), and Benue (-5.49 percent) recorded the slowest rise in Food inflation on a Month-on-Month basis.” Vanguard News The post Inflation rate drops year-on-year, rises month-on-month appeared first on Vanguard News .

NDC governorship candidate in Kano, Aminu Gwarzo, had alleged that during a campaign visit to Bichi on Sunday, the convoy of the vice presidential candidate of the party was attacked by thugs allegedly sent by the state government. The spokesperson for Gwarzo’s campaign, Ibrahim Shu’aibu, said the team had earlier visited Tofa, Rimingado, Kabo, Gwarzo, Shanono and Bagwai local government areas without disruption before proceeding to Bichi where they were attcked. But reacting to the attack, yesterday, the Commissioner for Information in Kano State, Sanusi Tofa, dismissed the fact that there was an attack on the convoy of Kwankwaso in Bichi Local Government Area, describing the incident as fictitious. Tofa, who accused the Kwankwasiyya Movement of fabricating the reported attack in Bichi said: “In an attempt to generate public sympathy, the Kwankwasiyya team has framed itself a fictitious attack in Bichi, no pictures, no videos.’’ Kano belongs to all, not those in power — Kwankwasiyya tells govt Replying the state government, the Kwankwasiyya Movement said Kano State belonged to all residents, regardless of their political affiliations. In a statement by its spokesperson, Dr Habibu Mohammed, yesterday, the movement also criticised the state government for dismissing the incident as fictitious and accusing the Kwankwasiyya Movement of making up the allegation to gain public sympathy. The statement specifically faulted the Commissioner for Information, Sanusi Tofa, for demanding pictures and videos of the incident, rather than allowing security agencies to investigate the matter. item.title: Aiding our traders to embrace manufacturing
item.description: Lagos State Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu’s call at the recent 19th China Commodities Expo and 40th Lagos International Trade Fair was timely. The governor urged traders to move beyond importing finished goods into local assembly, manufacturing, agro-processing and exports. He challenged Chinese investors to establish factories, transfer technology and partner with Nigerian businesses. The message is sound. But it collides with a business environment that makes production punishingly difficult. Nigeria remains heavily dependent on imported manufactured goods, while exporting too little value-added output. The Manufacturers Association of Nigeria, MAN, recently noted that manufactured goods accounted for only N2.5 trillion, or 2.94 per cent, of the N85.13 trillion in total exports recorded in 2025. The NESG has warned that manufacturing’s contribution to GDP is declining, with energy costs, import competition, inadequate finance and weak industrial coordination suppressing productive capacity. NESG’s October 2026 business monitor identified power outages, costly inputs, poor infrastructure, limited credit and raw-material shortages. Traders understandably gravitate towards importing. Chinese producers enjoy scale, technology, cheaper finance, reliable power and efficient logistics. A Nigerian entrepreneur contemplating a factory faces expensive electricity, high interest rates, volatile foreign exchange, costly machinery and inputs, multiple taxation, port delays, poor roads, smuggling and unpredictable regulations. Policy reversals and overlapping levies make long-term investment hazardous. It is easier and often more profitable to import a container than build a factory whose costs may overwhelm its owner. That is why government must do the heavy lifting. The NESG, NACCIMA and MAN have demanded policy consistency, affordable energy, accessible long-term finance, efficient infrastructure, simpler taxation, predictable trade rules and protection against dumping and substandard imports. These are not special favours; they are foundations of competitive production. President Bola Tinubu’s Nigeria First policy, directing public institutions to prioritise Nigerian-made goods, must become enforceable procurement practice, not a slogan. Government should publish compliance records, pay local suppliers promptly and enforce quality standards. It must expand industrial power through gas, embedded generation and renewables, lower financing costs through development banks, clear port bottlenecks, support research, skills and technology transfer, and provide stable incentives for investors who create local value and jobs, with transparent eligibility rules and measurable local-content targets. Traders should respond through joint ventures, contract manufacturing and gradual local assembly, rather than wait to become industrial giants overnight. item.title: Why must the opposition campaign in fear while the ruling party campaigns freely? By Ejiro Ofoye
item.description: There is something fundamentally wrong with a democracy when political parties cannot freely organise meetings, hold rallies, address citizens or mobilise supporters without the fear of being attacked. Nigeria is supposed to be a constitutional democracy, not a country where political power determines who enjoys the freedom to assemble and who must conduct political activities under the threat of violence. The increasing reports of attacks against opposition political parties, particularly the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), in Delta State, Lagos, Enugu, Benue and other parts of the country should worry every Nigerian. What is unfolding is embarrassing, dangerous and completely unacceptable in a country preparing for another general election. The situation is becoming so alarming that Nigerians must begin to ask whether the country is gradually approaching an election season in which political participation will be determined not by the strength of ideas, manifestoes and candidates, but by the capacity of political parties to deploy violence and intimidation. On October 10, 2026, during activities surrounding the governorship campaign flag-off of the NDC in Enugu State, suspected political attackers reportedly invaded areas where party supporters had gathered, including the campaign office of the party’s governorship candidate, Sir Christian Chinyeaka Ohaa, in the Government Reserved Area of Enugu. The violence resulted in gunshot injuries, damaged vehicles and the eventual death of an NDC supporter, Ifeanyi Nwolie. The Enugu State Government initially disputed reports of a fatality. However, subsequent reporting by Premium Times confirmed that Nwolie died from injuries sustained during the attack and was buried on October 22, 2026. The police had earlier announced an investigation into the shooting and directed its State Criminal Investigation Department to identify and apprehend the perpetrators. This is no longer an ordinary political disagreement. A Nigerian citizen has lost his life in an incident connected with political activities. What could be more disturbing than a situation in which a citizen cannot safely welcome a political candidate or participate in a political gathering? In Delta State, the experience has been equally disturbing. On September 18, 2026, the NDC’s One Million March in Warri and Effurun was disrupted by suspected political thugs. The confrontation reportedly occurred at different locations, including Airport Road, Ogboroke and Jakpa Junction. Participants sustained injuries, and there were disturbing accounts of weapons being displayed during the confrontation. What makes the incident particularly troubling is the allegation by participants that security personnel were present but failed to intervene promptly as the attackers confronted NDC members. item.title: Abia approves ₦1.04bn for SMEs, reviews ASEPA workers’ pay
item.description: …₦382.9m disbursed to 31 businesses By Steve Oko UMUAHIA — Abia State Government has secured approval for ₦1.041 billion in intervention funding for small and medium-scale enterprises (SMEs), in a move aimed at expanding businesses, stimulating job creation and improving access to affordable credit. Of the amount, ₦382.9 million has already been disbursed to 29 micro-enterprises and two small and medium-scale businesses, while another ₦206.7 million in approved applications is undergoing documentation ahead of disbursement. The state government also announced a review of the remuneration of ad-hoc workers engaged by the Abia State Environmental Protection Agency (ASEPA), with the new payment structure taking effect from November 2026. Commissioner for Information, Prince Okey Kanu, who disclosed the developments during the weekly briefing on the State Executive Council meeting at Government House, Umuahia, said the SME intervention was being implemented through the Bank of Industry (BOI). Kanu, represented by the Special Adviser to the Governor on Media and Publicity, Mr Fredinald Ekeoma, said the initiative was part of Governor Alex Otti’s administration’s efforts to strengthen the state’s productive sector and create sustainable employment opportunities. Providing further details, Commissioner for Industries and SMEs, Mazi Mike Akpara, said the outstanding approved facilities would be released once beneficiaries fulfilled the necessary conditions, including documentation and provision of guarantors and collateral, where applicable. He stressed that access to the intervention was not restricted by political affiliation, insisting that any genuine business operating in Abia was eligible. “Whether you belong to the Labour Party, PDP or APC, we are not concerned about that. Once you are doing business in Abia and can provide evidence of your business operations, you are eligible to benefit. “SMEs are the engine of the economy, and this initiative is intended to encourage and strengthen them,” Akpara said. He said interested businesses could access the programme through the Ministry of Industries and SMEs at the Nnamdi Azikiwe Secretariat, Umuahia, or the BOI office in Aba. Akpara described the facility as a major relief for local entrepreneurs, given its relatively low interest rates of 8.5 per cent for overdrafts and 7.5 per cent for other facilities, with a three-year repayment period. He contrasted the rates with commercial bank lending rates, which he said could rise to between 28 and 30 per cent, arguing that the intervention would ease the financing burden on businesses and improve their capacity to expand. In another development, Kanu said the Ministry of Industries and SMEs had verified and documented more than 110 workshops and 120 shops at the Ohiya-Umuogo-Nsukwe Industrial Cluster. item.title: Dry season farming: Shettima directs swift release of 3m fertiliser bags nationwide
item.description: ‎—Orders ONSA to monitor declared stocks ahead of distribution ‎ ‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ‎ ‎ABUJA — THE Vice President Senator Kashim Shettima has directed relevant government agencies and stakeholders in the fertiliser industry to expedite arrangements for the production and release of over three million bags of fertiliser to farmers across the country ahead of the forthcoming dry-season farming. ‎ ‎The directive followed President Bola Tinubu’s approval of funding under the Renewed Hope Agricultural Stabilisation and Productivity Initiative, aimed at making fertiliser more affordable, boosting food production and reviving Nigeria’s fertiliser blending industry. ‎ ‎The Vice President gave the directive on Monday at the Presidential Villa during a meeting with stakeholders in the fertiliser sector in Abuja, where the Fertiliser Producers and Suppliers Association of Nigeria (FEPSAN) disclosed that available raw materials could support the production of approximately three million bags of NPK fertiliser within the next few weeks. ‎ ‎He also directed the Office of the National Security Adviser (ONSA) to verify and track fertiliser stocks declared by stakeholders to ensure transparency, accountability and a hitch-free distribution exercise. ‎ ‎He further urged the NSA’s office to ensure that farming communities in states facing security challenges are not neglected in the distribution programme, stressing the need for the intervention to reach farmers in vulnerable and hard-to-access areas. ‎ ‎Speaking on the broader economic importance of the presidential intervention, the Vice President said revitalising Nigeria’s fertiliser industry would strengthen agricultural productivity while creating jobs and supporting rural livelihoods. ‎ ‎”A strong fertilizer value chain supports hundreds of thousands of direct and indirect jobs. item.title: Wike to opposition: Stop creating chaos to blame Tinubu
item.description: Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, FCT, Mr Nyesom Wike, yesterday, accused opposition political parties of deliberately fomenting trouble to make it appear that President Bola Tinubu is responsible for political violence ahead of the 2027 elections. Wike made the allegation during the inauguration of the All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council (APC-PCC) in the FCT at the Bola Ahmed Tinubu International Conference Centre in Abuja. The minister, who expressed confidence in the APC’s chances in the upcoming elections, claimed that opposition parties knew they had already lost and were creating political tension to discredit the ruling party. Wike said: “You have what it takes to win this election. The other parties know. Let me just tell you the simple truth. The other parties know they have lost the election. “What are they doing now? What they are doing now is to foment crisis—foment problems to make it look as if it is the government; it is the presidential candidate of the APC party who is fomenting trouble. “They (opposition) are the ones causing trouble. You (APC PCC) don’t need to cause trouble because you have already won the election. “They (opposition parties) foment trouble and report as if they are not the ones that have created that problem. So, we must be on alert.” Wike also told members of the Rainbow Coalition to make sure the African Democratic Congress, ADC, and the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, do not get 25 per cent of the votes in the FCT in the January 16, 2027 general elections. He warned the members against assuming the contest was already won, saying the election was a chance for the APC to show its political strength in the territory. On how to sell the president’s record, he said: “You don’t need to go and see a prophet. You don’t need to go and see any doctor or anybody to tell you what to do. It is obvious; it is factual. Look at what Mr President has done for the people of the FCT. These are the tools you need to campaign.” Wike also dared opposition politicians to set projects built before 2023 beside those delivered since Tinubu took office, arguing that the work going on in the city centre and the satellite towns spoke for itself. item.title: Justice Lifu’s judgment, Atiku’s fate and the road to 2027
item.description: By Tunde Rahman Some judgments settle a dispute. Some judgments can reorder a nation’s politics. The judgment delivered on November 5, 2026, by Justice Peter Lifu of the Federal High Court, Abuja, in Suit No. FHC/ABJ/CS/1819/2025 – Nafiu Bala Gombe versus African Democratic Congress and Others – belongs to the second category. That judgment did not just decide who leads a party. It has placed former Vice President Atiku Abubakar’s presidential ambition and the future of the ADC in suspense, and perhaps created a crisis of perception for the 2027 general election. What did the court actually decide? Let me state from the get-go that neither the All Progressives Congress nor President Bola Tinubu filed the case. A member of the ADC itself– Nafiu Bala Gombe, the former Deputy National Chairman (North-East), – filed it. Gombe argued that after the former National Chairman, Ralph Nwosu, resigned, leadership should have devolved to him under the party’s constitution. Instead, he argued, a caretaker leadership led by former Senate President David Mark and former Osun Governor Rauf Aregbesola was imposed at the 99th National Executive Committee meeting on July 27, 2025, without a democratic election. Justice Lifu agreed with him. Among other things, the judge held that David Mark’s emergence as National Chairman and Rauf Aregbesola’s emergence as National Secretary were unlawful. He also stated that Nafiu Bala Gombe’s purported resignation letter was fictitious. After comparing the signatures on the letter with Gombe’s sworn witness statements, the judge found material differences and held that the document could not be relied upon. Justice Lifu then ordered that all actions, decisions, and steps taken by the David Mark-led National Working Committee from July 27, 2025, are null, void, and without effect, and that the Independent National Electoral Commission should not recognise the Mark-led leadership. The legal anchor was Section 82 (3) of the Electoral Act 2022, which requires political parties to elect their officers democratically. According to Justice Lifu, neither a NEC resolution nor INEC’s administrative recognition could substitute for that statutory requirement. This is how the judgment affects former Vice President Atiku Abubakar. Admittedly, Atiku was not a party to the suit, and his name, according to his lawyers, was not expressly mentioned in the operative orders after the Certified True Copy was finally released on Wednesday, November 11. But this logic is consequential. If the leadership that conducted the ADC presidential primary was essentially invalid, then the primary it conducted is also called into question. That is why news media reports from the judgment concluded that the process that produced Atiku as the ADC presidential candidate for the January 16, 2027 election has been invalidated. item.title: 2027: APC rallies deepening Nigerians’ anger, Kawu warns party leaders
item.description: …Senator decries disconnect between northern masses and political elite, urges grassroots mobilisation By Henry Umoru ABUJA — Chairman of the Senate Committee on Petroleum (Downstream), Senator Kawu Sumaila Suleiman (APC, Kano South), has warned the leadership of the All Progressives Congress (APC) that displays of opulence, celebrations and merrymaking at presidential campaign rallies are deepening the pains and anger of Nigerians. The senator, who is the APC senatorial candidate for the January 16, 2027 election, said there was a growing disconnect and misunderstanding between ordinary people in the North and the political elite. In a statement addressed to party leaders and members on Monday, his second intervention on the matter, Suleiman called for a change in the party’s approach and strategy ahead of the 2027 general elections. He urged the APC leadership and Presidential Campaign Council (PCC) to prioritise effective communication of President Bola Tinubu’s policies and ongoing reforms to Nigerians at the grassroots. The lawmaker also called on the party to identify and empower credible individuals and stakeholders with genuine grassroots influence in their respective constituencies rather than relying on what he described as “Abuja politicians” and entitled individuals disconnected from the people. In the statement titled, “A Clarion Call for Self-Reflection, Humility, and Grassroots Reconnection”, Suleiman said the party’s message was still not reaching ordinary Nigerians. He said: “Following my earlier message, we must once again be completely honest with ourselves: our message is still not reaching the grassroots. We need to acknowledge and accept that there is a growing disconnect and misunderstanding between the common people in the North and the political elites. We must change our approach and strategy. “There is an urgent need to effectively communicate our government’s policies and the ongoing reforms of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu directly to the grassroots.” The senator warned that the celebratory atmosphere at campaign rallies was insensitive to the hardship and insecurity confronting many Nigerians, particularly in the North. item.title: Why growing communities deserve fair electoral structure
item.description: By Christopher Nwayalani In a democracy, political representation should reflect the realities of the people. As a community expands in population, geography and economic importance, its electoral structures deserve periodic examination to ensure that the citizenry enjoys fair, equitable and meaningful representation. Where existing arrangements appear inadequate to reflect changing circumstances, the responsible response should be a lawful, evidence-based review. This is the central issue behind the growing call for equitable political representation for Okpanam Kingdom, a rapidly developing community in Oshimili North Local Government Area of Delta State. On Saturday, November 7, 2026, the people of Okpanam took a strategic and significant step in articulating this aspiration when traditional rulers, community leaders, political stakeholders, professionals, youths, women and members of the diaspora gathered at the Ugo Ani Palace Hall for the Okpanam Political Summit 2026. Organised with the theme, “Equitable Political Representation for a Growing Okpanam: The Imperative of INEC Electoral Delineation and the Creation of Additional Wards,” the summit provided a platform for constructive engagement over the relationship between the community’s meteoric growth and expansion as well as its current electoral arrangement. The gathering was more than a discussion about political boundaries. It was a call for responsible community advocacy, democratic fairness and a development process driven by credible evidence rather than sentiment. A growing urban community Okpanam has witnessed remarkable transformation over the last two decades and a half. Its growth is reflected in expanding residential estates, emerging neighbourhoods, economic and commercial activities and increasing population. Areas such as Obodogba, Ogbeozoma, Amachai and Ogbogwugwu, alongside several new estates and residential layouts, illustrate the wholesome evolving character of the community. What was once largely regarded as a traditional settlement on the outskirts of Asaba has increasingly become part of the expanding urban landscape of the Delta State capital territory. The transformation did not only bring opportunities, but also created new demands on infrastructure, public services, planning and democratic representation. The fundamental question is whether the existing electoral arrangement adequately reflects the community’s present realities. For the people of Okpanam, this question deserves serious consideration by the relevant government authorities and agencies. Political representation is not merely about occupying elective positions. It determines how effectively communities participate in decision-making, articulate their needs and engage with government and government institutions. item.title: Don’t turn churches into campaign arena, Soludo cautions politicians
item.description: By Vincent Ujumadu Governor Charles Soludo of Anambra State, on Sunday, cautioned politicians against turning churches and other places of worship into a political arena, stating that sacred spaces must remain neutral grounds for people of all political persuasions. Soludo made the remark during the 30th anniversary celebration of the Mountain of Holy Ghost Intervention and Deliverance Ministry founded by Prophet Chukwuemeka Ohanaemere, popularly known as Odumeje. Addressing the congregation, the governor stressed the need for the men of God to clearly separate politics from worship. According to Soludo, the place of worship should be a holy place where people of all political persuasion should come and worship God in peace. “It should not be a place for politics. There is a venue for politics. If you want to worship God, you have to go to the house of God. We must separate the two things clearly,” Soludo said. He recalled that six months before his election, he took a deliberate decision never to go to any church to cup a microphone to ask them to vote for him or to campaign. “It was a deliberate decision. I worshipped in the government house chapel until the election day and afterwards,” the governor stated. “We must never politicise the church. We must never politicise the place of worship. Politicians, keep off churches. Keep off places of worship. That’s a deliberate message, and it is my kind of consistency of character”, he further said. item.title: 2027 Elections: ‘Nigerians Have Been Rejecting Him,’ Segun Sowunmi Faults Atiku’s Candidacy
item.description: A Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) chieftain, Segun Sowunmi, has criticised African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate Atiku Abubakar’s repeated bids for Nigeria’s presidency, claiming that Nigerians have consistently rejected his ambition at the polls. Sowunmi, who is also a member of the All Progressives Congress (APC) campaign council, made the remarks on Monday during an appearance on Channels Television’s Politics Today . Responding to a question about Atiku’s belief that he is better positioned than President Bola Tinubu to govern Nigeria, Sowunmi said the former vice president should reconsider his ambition. “Well, he’s been saying that for a while, and Nigerians have been rejecting him,” he said. FILES: Segun Sowunmi on Channels Television’s Politics Today “If you have done elections the number of times Waziri (Atiku) has done, there is something he himself must consider. At what point in time does he expect younger, sharper northern people to get tired or be fatigued at running around with him?” he asked. North Presidency Calculations The PDP chieftain, who was a spokesperson for the Atiku Abubakar Presidential Campaign Organisation in 2023, also questioned the former vice president’s political calculations, noting that the North had already produced a president who governed for eight years under former President Muhammadu Buhari. He further questioned Atiku’s candidacy under the African Democratic Congress (ADC), following a Federal High Court judgment nullifying the leadership of the caretaker committee led by former Senate President David Mark. The November 5 judgment, delivered by Justice Peter Lifu in Abuja, followed a suit filed by Nafiu Bala Gombe, a former deputy national chairman of the ADC, challenging the emergence of the Mark-led leadership. Atiku Abubakar is the presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress for the 2027 general elections. The ruling affected decisions taken by the committee, including the process that produced Atiku as the party’s 2027 presidential candidate. The ADC group has rejected the judgment and appealed. Sowunmi, however, maintained that Atiku’s candidacy remained uncertain. “As at today, he is not on the ballot. Because you appeal a case you lost in the lower court, does that mean you are going to win it? The bottom line is that, as at today, he is not their candidate,” he said. He also accused Atiku of mishandling the dispute involving Gombe, describing his approach as an “emir complex”. “Emirs don’t beg, emirs don’t visit people, call others. Emirs sit at home, and everybody comes to meet them. Yes, you can be an emir, but you can’t be an emir if you are looking for a ticket in another man’s party,” he added. item.title: [VIDEO] Bamayi: I’m Extremely Disappointed Security Agencies Allow That Joke To Go On — Sowunmi
item.description: A chieftain of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), Segun Sowunmi, has condemned the recent ‘Bamayi’ protest in Abuja, expressing disappointment with security agencies over their handling of the incident. Sowunmi, who is also a member of the All Progressives Congress (APC) campaign council, made the remarks on Monday during an appearance on Channels Television’s Politics Today. He criticised the destruction of campaign posters and the use of violence by protesters who chanted ‘Bamayi’ at President Bola Tinubu’s motorcade, describing such actions as undemocratic. “I am disappointed, extremely disappointed that security is allowing that kind of joke to go on under the guise of people who are running democracy,” he said. Sowunmi argued that Nigerians dissatisfied with a political candidate or campaign should express their opposition through the ballot box rather than resorting to violence. “I expect people who have a point of view different from that of a campaign to wait until the day of election to exercise their franchise. But to be destroying people’s posters, to be carrying sticks and running up and down, that’s for barbarians, and I don’t expect any sane leader to do that,” he added. The ‘Bamayi’ chants, which translate to ‘we don’t want’ in Hausa, were heard on November 13 after President Tinubu attended Friday prayers at the Shehu Shagari Mosque in the Garki area of Abuja. Some protesters reportedly threw stones at the President’s convoy and destroyed APC campaign posters, prompting security operatives to intervene.
